description: Breakaway denominations ordered by start/rupture year (groups_catalog + unique denominations_extra).

denominations.name: Novatianists
denominations.summary: Rigorist schism over lapsi; lasting parallel hierarchy for centuries.

denominations.name: Melitian schism (Egypt)
denominations.summary: Egyptian rigorist schism contemporary with early Arian controversies.

denominations.name: Donatists
denominations.summary: North African rigorist church rejecting traditor clergy and Catholic episcopal legitimacy.

denominations.name: Arian churches
denominations.summary: Communities and royal churches refusing Nicene homoousios; Homoean/Arian ecclesial structures among Goths, Vandals, Lombards.

denominations.name: Church of the East (Assyrian Church of the East)
denominations.summary: East Syriac dyophysite patriarchate that did not accept Ephesus’s condemnation of Nestorius; modern English name often ‘Assyrian Church of the East’.

denominations.name: Armenian Apostolic Church
denominations.summary: National church rejecting Chalcedon; later Florence union attempt with Armenians.

denominations.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
denominations.summary: Alexandrian miaphysite patriarchate after Chalcedon; head of much African Oriental Orthodoxy.

denominations.name: Syriac Orthodox Church
denominations.summary: West Syriac miaphysite patriarchate of Antioch (Jacobite).

denominations.name: Eastern Orthodox churches
denominations.summary: Byzantine-rite autocephalous churches out of full communion with Rome after the East–West schism.

denominations.name: Waldensians
denominations.summary: Poor of Lyons dissenting movement forming lasting communities; later joined Reformed Protestantism.

denominations.name: Wycliffites / Lollards
denominations.summary: English Wycliffite/Lollard reform networks condemned at Constance.

denominations.name: Hussites
denominations.summary: Bohemian reform communion after Hus; Utraquist and Taborite wings.

denominations.name: Unitas Fratrum / Moravian Church
denominations.summary: Bohemian Brethren emerging from Hussite reform; renewed at Herrnhut as Moravian Church.

denominations.name: Lutheran churches
denominations.summary: Evangelical churches of the Augsburg Confession rejecting papal jurisdiction and Tridentine soteriology/sacraments.

denominations.name: Reformed / Calvinist churches
denominations.summary: Magisterial Reformed communions (Zwinglian/Calvinist) rejecting Roman jurisdiction and Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Anabaptist / Radical Reformation churches
denominations.summary: Radical Reformation bodies practicing believers’ baptism and often separation from magisterial churches.

denominations.name: Hutterites
denominations.summary: Communal Anabaptist tradition under Jakob Hutter.

denominations.name: Anglican Communion / Church of England
denominations.summary: English national church rejecting papal jurisdiction; later Anglican Communion provinces.

denominations.name: Mennonite churches
denominations.summary: Anabaptist tradition associated with Menno Simons; multiple conferences worldwide.

denominations.name: Church of Scotland
denominations.summary: National Presbyterian church; rejects papal jurisdiction and Trent.

denominations.name: Presbyterian churches
denominations.summary: Reformed churches with Presbyterian polity (e.g. Church of Scotland). Generally the Scottish/English form of the Reformed Reformation, not a later schism *from* continental Reformed churches.

denominations.name: Unitarian / Unitarian Universalist churches
denominations.summary: Anti-Trinitarian and later liberal Protestant churches. Anglo-American Unitarianism grew mainly from Congregational/Separatist settings; Transylvanian Unitarianism is an earlier, separate continental stream.

denominations.name: English Separatists / Congregationalists
denominations.summary: Separatist and non-separating Puritan congregational churches leaving Anglican settlement.

denominations.name: Baptist churches
denominations.summary: Believers’-baptism churches emerging from English Separatism (General/Particular Baptists); later global family.

denominations.name: General Baptists
denominations.summary: Arminian Baptists; believers’ baptism against infant baptism and Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Remonstrant Brotherhood
denominations.summary: Dutch Arminian (Remonstrant) churches organized after the Synod of Dort (1618–19) condemned the Remonstrant articles and expelled Arminian ministers from the Dutch Reformed Church.

denominations.name: Reformed Church in America
denominations.summary: Dutch Reformed in America; Protestant against Trent and papal primacy.

denominations.name: Particular Baptists
denominations.summary: Calvinistic Baptists; believers’ baptism and Reformed soteriology against infant baptism and Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Scottish Covenanters
denominations.summary: National Covenant / rejection of episcopacy and royal liturgical impositions in Scotland.

denominations.name: Seventh Day Baptist churches
denominations.summary: Sabbatarian Baptists; earlier than Seventh-day Adventists.

denominations.name: Religious Society of Friends (Quakers)
denominations.summary: Fox’s Friends movement arising in the English Civil War religious ferment.

denominations.name: Priestless Old Believers (Bespopovtsy)
denominations.summary: Old Believer priestless wing; reject Nikonian (and by extension Latinizing) liturgical settlement.

denominations.name: Russian Old Believers
denominations.summary: Split from Russian Orthodoxy over Nikonian liturgical reforms; popovtsy and bespopovtsy wings.

denominations.name: Amish
denominations.summary: Jakob Ammann split from Swiss Mennonites over discipline and shunning.

denominations.name: Church of the Brethren (Schwarzenau Brethren)
denominations.summary: Schwarzenau Brethren (German Baptists / Dunkers) formed 1708 under Alexander Mack with believers’ baptism and Anabaptist-Pietist practice; distinct from Mennonite conferences.

denominations.name: Moravian Church (Unitas Fratrum worldwide)
denominations.summary: Herrnhut renewal of Unitas Fratrum; Protestant against papal and Tridentine claims.

denominations.name: United Society of Believers (Shakers)
denominations.summary: Celibate communal restorationism; reject historic sacramental and hierarchical Catholic order.

denominations.name: Doukhobors
denominations.summary: Russian Spiritual Christian; reject sacraments and clergy as Catholic/Orthodox churches define them.

denominations.name: Molokans
denominations.summary: Russian Spiritual Christian dissent; reject Orthodox/Catholic ritual and hierarchy.

denominations.name: Brethren in Christ Church
denominations.summary: Anabaptist-Pietist; believers’ baptism against Catholic infant baptism and hierarchy.

denominations.name: Free Will Baptist churches (National Association of Free Will Baptists)
denominations.summary: Arminian (‘General’ / Free Will) Baptist stream distinct from Particular/Calvinistic Baptists; northern and southern Free Will bodies united in the National Association of Free Will Baptists (1935).

denominations.name: Associate Reformed Presbyterian Church
denominations.summary: Scottish-American Reformed; Protestant against Trent and papacy.

denominations.name: Methodist churches
denominations.summary: Wesleyan movement that formed separate churches from Anglican structures.

denominations.name: Swedenborgian / New Church
denominations.summary: New Church / Swedenborgian bodies organized from the late 18th century, especially in England, on the basis of Emanuel Swedenborg’s writings.

denominations.name: Petite Église (anticoncordataires)
denominations.summary: Clergy and faithful who refused the 1801 Concordat between Napoleon and Pius VII (and related reorganizations), maintaining a small separated ‘Little Church’ in parts of France and neighboring regions.

denominations.name: Restoration Movement (Stone–Campbell)
denominations.summary: American restorationists seeking New Testament church pattern; Churches of Christ / Christian Churches / Disciples.

denominations.name: Cumberland Presbyterian Church
denominations.summary: Revivalist Presbyterian; Protestant against Trent and papacy.

denominations.name: Primitive Methodist Church
denominations.summary: Hugh Bourne / William Clowes camp-meeting Methodists, excluded from Wesleyan Methodist Connexion structures, organized the Primitive Methodist Connexion (1811).

denominations.name: African Methodist Episcopal Church
denominations.summary: Black Methodist denomination founded by Richard Allen amid racial exclusion.

denominations.name: African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church
denominations.summary: Independent Black Methodist body formed in New York.

denominations.name: Plymouth Brethren
denominations.summary: Restorationist evangelical assemblies rejecting denominationalism; Open and Exclusive wings.

denominations.name: Open Brethren
denominations.summary: Open Brethren; reject Catholic priesthood and sacramental system.

denominations.name: Apostolic Christian Church
denominations.summary: Froehlich Anabaptist; believers’ baptism and separation from Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
denominations.summary: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints founded by Joseph Smith as a restoration of primitive Christianity, not as a schism from the Stone–Campbell Restoration Movement.

denominations.name: Dutch Reformed secession churches (Afscheiding/Doleantie)
denominations.summary: 19th-c. orthodox secessions from state Dutch Reformed Church; roots of CRCNA/Gereformeerde kerken.

denominations.name: Catholic Apostolic Church (Irvingite)
denominations.summary: Apostolic restorationist body associated with Edward Irving and the Albury circle; organized with restored ‘apostles’ (c. 1835). Grew from Church of Scotland / Presbyterian and broader Protestant apocalyptic circles.

denominations.name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church
denominations.summary: Reformed Oriental/West Syriac church influenced by Anglican CMS; distinct from both Rome and Malankara Orthodoxy.

denominations.name: Free Church of Scotland
denominations.summary: Evangelical majority left the established Church of Scotland in the 1843 Disruption over spiritual independence and patronage, forming the Free Church of Scotland.

denominations.name: Wesleyan Church
denominations.summary: Wesleyan-Holiness denomination with roots in abolitionist Methodist splits.

denominations.name: Millerite / Adventist movement
denominations.summary: Second Great Awakening advent expectation; parent of Seventh-day Adventists and other advent bodies. Mixed Baptist/Christian Connexion roots.

denominations.name: Southern Baptist Convention
denominations.summary: US Baptist split over slavery/missions organization; largest US Protestant denomination historically.

denominations.name: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod
denominations.summary: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod organized (1847) by Saxon and other Lutheran immigrants in the U.S.; not founded as a schism from a single existing Lutheran synod abroad.

denominations.name: Exclusive Brethren (Darbyite)
denominations.summary: Darbyite Exclusive assemblies separating from Open Brethren.

denominations.name: Wisconsin Evangelical Lutheran Synod
denominations.summary: Confessional Lutheran; rejects Trent on justification, Mass, and papal primacy.

denominations.name: Christian Reformed Church in North America
denominations.summary: Dutch Reformed immigrants in Michigan seceded from the Reformed Church in America (1857), forming what became the Christian Reformed Church; linked to Afscheiding confessional concerns.

denominations.name: Advent Christian Church
denominations.summary: Conditionalist Adventist denomination organized from Millerite advent believers who did not accept Seventh-day Adventist distinctive doctrines (Sabbath, EGW, sanctuary).

denominations.name: Community of Christ (RLDS)
denominations.summary: Reorganized Latter Day Saint church under Joseph Smith III lineage.

denominations.name: Free Methodist Church
denominations.summary: Holiness Methodist split emphasizing free pews and sanctification.

denominations.name: Chaldean Syrian Church of India
denominations.summary: East Syriac Indian church; dyophysite against Cyrilline Ephesine settlement.

denominations.name: Church of Christ (Temple Lot)
denominations.summary: Hedrickite Latter Day Saint body rejecting Brigham Young and plural marriage; claims the Independence Temple Lot and a restored church without Utah LDS developments.

denominations.name: New Apostolic Church
denominations.summary: Hamburg-centered continuation that called further apostles after conflict with remaining Catholic Apostolic apostles (1863); grew into the global New Apostolic Church.

denominations.name: Seventh-day Adventist Church
denominations.summary: Sabbatarian Adventist denomination organized after the Great Disappointment.

denominations.name: Salvation Army
denominations.summary: Booth’s Wesleyan mission that became a distinct quasi-military church organization.

denominations.name: Holiness movement churches
denominations.summary: Wesleyan-holiness denominations emphasizing entire sanctification (e.g. Church of the Nazarene roots, Pilgrim Holiness).

denominations.name: Christian Methodist Episcopal Church
denominations.summary: Black Methodist church organized from the Methodist Episcopal Church, South.

denominations.name: Old Catholic churches (Union of Utrecht)
denominations.summary: Communions rejecting Vatican I papal infallibility/primacy definitions.

denominations.name: Old Order Mennonites
denominations.summary: Mennonite groups that refused progressive innovations (meetinghouses, revivalism, later technology) and retained older Ordnung discipline; distinct from the Amish though parallel in conservatism.

denominations.name: Reformed Episcopal Church
denominations.summary: Evangelical Anglican body founded by Bishop George David Cummins and others leaving the Protestant Episcopal Church over ritualism and catholicizing trends.

denominations.name: Bible Student movement
denominations.summary: Russell’s Bible Student movement emerging from adventist/restorationist milieu.

denominations.name: Church of Christ, Scientist
denominations.summary: Church of Christ, Scientist founded by Mary Baker Eddy (1879) in New England Protestant culture; not a clean jurisdictional schism from a single denomination.

denominations.name: Church of God (Anderson)
denominations.summary: Holiness restorationist movement under D. S. Warner.

denominations.name: Evangelical Covenant Church
denominations.summary: Swedish Mission Covenant / Mission Friends free-church movement arising from Lutheran revivalism; American Evangelical Covenant Church continues that stream.

denominations.name: Church of God (Cleveland, Tennessee)
denominations.summary: Holiness church begun in the R. G. Spurling / A. J. Tomlinson stream (1886); became a major classical Pentecostal denomination after Azusa-era Spirit baptism teaching.

denominations.name: Christian and Missionary Alliance
denominations.summary: Simpson’s deeper-life missionary movement becoming a denomination.

denominations.name: Evangelical Friends Church International
denominations.summary: Gurneyite / evangelical Friends who adopted programmed worship, pastors, and evangelical doctrine, distinct from silent unprogrammed Liberal/Hicksite Friends.

denominations.name: Unity Church
denominations.summary: New Thought; rejects Catholic sacramental realism and dogma.

denominations.name: National Baptist Convention, USA
denominations.summary: Major African American Baptist convention organized 1895 from earlier Black Baptist mission/publishing unions—parallel to white Baptist conventions rather than a single congregational secession.

denominations.name: General Church of the New Jerusalem
denominations.summary: Swedenborgian New Church body; rejects Nicene-Catholic dogma as received in favor of Swedenborg’s revelations.

denominations.name: Polish National Catholic Church
denominations.summary: Independent Catholic jurisdiction among Polish immigrants; historically allied with Old Catholics.

denominations.name: Friends United Meeting
denominations.summary: Quaker; reject outward sacraments as Catholic churches define them.

denominations.name: Philippine Independent Church (Aglipayan)
denominations.summary: National church separating from Rome under Gregorio Aglipay amid colonial transition.

denominations.name: American Baptist Association
denominations.summary: Landmark Baptist fellowship organized after withdrawal from Southern Baptist Convention structures over local-church authority, closed communion, and opposition to centralized denominationalism (Baptist General Association → ABA).

denominations.name: Christian Church (Disciples of Christ)
denominations.approx_rupture: 1906 (US Census recognition of Restoration three-way split)
denominations.summary: Open-membership, instrumental Restoration wing that became the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ), distinguished from a cappella Churches of Christ after the early-20th-century Restoration division.

denominations.name: Churches of Christ (a cappella)
denominations.summary: Conservative Restoration branch opposing instruments and missionary societies.

denominations.name: Mariavite Church (Old Catholic Church of the Mariavites)
denominations.summary: Polish Catholic renewal movement around Feliksa Kozłowska; suppressed and leaders excommunicated (1906), then organized as an independent church (later allied with Utrecht Old Catholics; majority body based in Płock).

denominations.name: Pentecostal churches
denominations.summary: Classical Pentecostal denominations emerging from Holiness revival (Azusa Street, etc.).

denominations.name: American Baptist Churches USA
denominations.summary: Baptist; believers’ baptism against Catholic infant baptism and hierarchy.

denominations.name: Church of God in Christ
denominations.summary: Major African American Pentecostal denomination under Charles H. Mason after Azusa Street; Holiness roots reorganized as Pentecostal COGIC.

denominations.name: Church of the Nazarene
denominations.summary: Major Holiness denomination consolidated from Methodist-holiness bodies.

denominations.name: Jacobite Syrian Christian Church (Malankara)
denominations.summary: Malankara church under the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch (Jacobite Syrian Christian Church), as distinct from the autocephalous Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

denominations.name: Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church
denominations.summary: Indian Orthodox church of West Syriac liturgy that asserted autocephaly vis-à-vis the Syriac Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch (1912).

denominations.name: Assemblies of God
denominations.summary: Largest classical Pentecostal fellowship, organized at Hot Springs, Arkansas.

denominations.name: Iglesia ni Cristo
denominations.summary: Restorationist church founded by Félix Manalo (registered 1914). Independent of the Philippine Independent Church; Manalo rejected Aglipayan doctrine as still essentially Catholic.

denominations.name: Liberal Catholic Church
denominations.summary: Theosophically influenced independent sacramental church deriving orders via Old Catholic lines.

denominations.name: Oneness Pentecostal churches
denominations.summary: Non-Trinitarian Pentecostal bodies (e.g. UPCI) splitting from Trinitarian Pentecostalism.

denominations.name: Czechoslovak Hussite Church
denominations.summary: Founded 8 January 1920 by reformist Roman Catholic clergy (Karel Farský et al.) after Vatican rejection of vernacular liturgy, voluntary celibacy, and related demands; claims Hussite heritage while originating as a Catholic clerical schism.

denominations.name: Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia (ROCOR)
denominations.summary: Emigré Russian Orthodox jurisdiction; reconciled with Moscow Patriarchate in 2007 though some splinters remain separate.

denominations.name: Kimbanguist Church
denominations.summary: Church of Jesus Christ on Earth by the Prophet Simon Kimbangu; arose among Baptist-mission Christians in the Belgian Congo and became an independent AIC.

denominations.name: Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church
denominations.summary: Ukrainian autocephaly against Moscow; still non-Roman, rejects Vatican I papal definitions.

denominations.name: Church of God of Prophecy
denominations.summary: Holiness-Pentecostal; rejects Catholic hierarchical and sacramental claims.

denominations.name: International Church of the Foursquare Gospel
denominations.summary: Pentecostal denomination founded by Aimee Semple McPherson (1923) with the ‘Foursquare’ gospel emphasis; distinct from Assemblies of God and other classical bodies.

denominations.name: Greek Old Calendarists
denominations.summary: Greek jurisdictions rejecting the Revised Julian calendar; subset of True Orthodox phenomenon.

denominations.name: True Orthodox / Old Calendarist churches
denominations.summary: Jurisdictions rejecting mainstream Orthodox calendar reforms and/or perceived ecumenism.

denominations.name: Aladura churches
denominations.summary: Yoruba prayer-healing (Aladura) churches in Nigeria emerging from Anglican and other Protestant mission settings (e.g. Christ Apostolic Church, Cherubim and Seraphim).

denominations.name: Seventh Day Adventist Reform Movement
denominations.summary: Sabbatarian Adventist reform body arising from World War I conflicts over military service and church discipline within European Seventh-day Adventism.

denominations.name: Centers for Spiritual Living
denominations.summary: Religious Science; rejects Catholic sacramental and hierarchical claims.

denominations.name: Christian Churches and Churches of Christ (Independent)
denominations.summary: Conservative instrumental Restoration congregations that refused Disciples denominational structures and theological liberalism, remaining as Independent Christian Churches / Churches of Christ (not the a cappella Churches of Christ).

denominations.name: Jehovah’s Witnesses
denominations.summary: Watch Tower society under Rutherford; distinct doctrines on Trinity, governance, eschatology.

denominations.name: Grace Communion International (ex-WCG)
denominations.summary: Armstrongite origins; historically rejected Catholic Trinity and festal calendar.

denominations.name: Grace Communion International (ex–Worldwide Church of God)
denominations.summary: Armstrong’s Radio/Worldwide Church of God; later trinitarian evangelical reformation as GCI; splinters remain.

denominations.name: Reformed Church in the United States
denominations.summary: German Reformed confessional body; Protestant against Trent and papal jurisdiction.

denominations.name: Catholic Mariavite Church (Felicjanów)
denominations.summary: Minority Mariavite body that remained with Archbishop Kowalski after the 1935 deposition dispute; headquartered at Felicjanów.

denominations.name: Orthodox Presbyterian Church
denominations.summary: Confessional Presbyterian church formed under J. Gresham Machen after conflict with the Presbyterian Church in the U.S.A. over modernism and foreign missions.

denominations.name: Bible Presbyterian Church
denominations.summary: Confessional Presbyterian separatist; rejects Trent and papal jurisdiction.

denominations.name: Charis Fellowship (Grace Brethren)
denominations.summary: Brethren; believers’ baptism and threefold communion against Catholic sacramental system.

denominations.name: Brazilian Catholic Apostolic Church
denominations.summary: Independent Catholic church founded by Carlos Duarte Costa.

denominations.name: United Pentecostal Church International
denominations.summary: Largest Oneness Pentecostal denomination, formed by merger of Pentecostal Church, Incorporated and Pentecostal Assemblies of Jesus Christ (1945).

denominations.name: Baptist Missionary Association of America
denominations.summary: Landmark Baptist body formed in 1950 when churches left the American Baptist Association (initially North American Baptist Association; renamed BMAA).

denominations.name: Evangelical Free Church
denominations.summary: Free-church evangelical tradition with Scandinavian Lutheran free-church ancestry.

denominations.name: Chinese Catholic Patriotic Association structures
denominations.summary: State-supervised Catholic structures with contested communion claims regarding Rome.

denominations.name: United Church of Christ
denominations.summary: US merger of Congregational Christian and Evangelical & Reformed churches.

denominations.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
denominations.approx_rupture: Coptic jurisdiction → autocephaly 1959 (miaphysite via Alexandria after 451)
denominations.summary: Tewahedo church historically under the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria; autocephalous since 1959. Miaphysite identity via Coptic / non-Chalcedonian lineage.

denominations.name: Independent Charismatic / neo-Pentecostal networks
denominations.summary: Post-classical charismatic megachurches and apostolic networks; many have mixed Protestant parentage.

denominations.name: Progressive National Baptist Convention
denominations.summary: Black Baptist convention formed in 1961 by leaders leaving the National Baptist Convention, USA, amid disputes over civil-rights activism and presidential tenure limits.

denominations.name: Calvary Chapel Association
denominations.summary: Chuck Smith’s Calvary Chapel movement emerging from Foursquare/Pentecostal contexts into an independent charismatic-evangelical association with distinctive verse-by-verse teaching and Jesus Movement outreach.

denominations.name: Ancient Church of the East
denominations.summary: Calendar/jurisdiction split from the Assyrian Church of the East.

denominations.name: United Methodist Church
denominations.summary: Mainline Methodist union; Protestant against papal primacy and Tridentine sacramental definitions.

denominations.name: Missionary Church
denominations.summary: Anabaptist-evangelical; believers’ baptism against Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Bible Methodist Connection of Churches
denominations.summary: Conservative Holiness Methodist body formed by congregations leaving the Wesleyan Church over perceived relaxation of Holiness standards after mid-20th-century mergers.

denominations.name: Sedevacantist independent chapels and societies
denominations.summary: Bodies holding the post-conciliar Holy See vacant; separate sacramental networks (e.g. CMRI, SSPV).

denominations.name: United Reformed Church
denominations.summary: UK Reformed union; Protestant against Catholic magisterium.

denominations.name: Presbyterian Church in America
denominations.summary: Conservative Presbyterian denomination formed chiefly from the Presbyterian Church in the United States (Southern) over biblical authority, confessional standards, and opposition to liberal trends.

denominations.name: Continuing Anglican churches
denominations.summary: Jurisdictions leaving Canterbury/ECUSA Communion over prayer book, ordination, and doctrinal changes (Congress of St. Louis).

denominations.name: Palmarian Catholic Church
denominations.summary: Conclavist church with its own papacy centered at El Palmar de Troya.

denominations.name: Evangelical Presbyterian Church
denominations.summary: Evangelical Presbyterian denomination formed mainly by congregations leaving the United Presbyterian Church / PC(USA) stream over theology, sexuality, and property/conscience issues, with an ‘essentials’ confessional approach.

denominations.name: Vineyard Movement
denominations.summary: Charismatic evangelical association founded by John Wimber et al.

denominations.name: Evangelical Lutheran Church in America
denominations.summary: Mainline Lutheran; justification and sacramental theology distinct from Tridentine Catholic definitions.

denominations.name: Cooperative Baptist Fellowship
denominations.summary: Baptist fellowship; Protestant against Catholic sacramental and papal claims.

denominations.name: Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church
denominations.summary: Autocephalous Oriental Orthodox church separated from Ethiopian Orthodox after Eritrean independence.

denominations.name: Free Church of Scotland (Continuing)
denominations.summary: Minority that left the Free Church of Scotland in 2000 amid worship and discipline controversies, claiming to continue historic Free Church practice.

denominations.name: Mennonite Church USA
denominations.summary: Anabaptist; believers’ baptism and peace church against Catholic sacramental order.

denominations.name: Anglican Church in North America
denominations.summary: Realignment province formed by conservatives leaving The Episcopal Church / ACC.
